title: The Wayward mindset
summary: Why other imbued fear the Wayward.

claims.text: Waywards pursue the hunt with an obsessive, often hateful drive and will do almost anything to see it through.
Each Wayward seems split between an ordinary, reasoning person and something colder and more childish, and the hunt is driven by the struggle between the two.

title: Wayward Conviction
summary: How Waywards regain and lose Conviction.

claims.text: A Wayward regains a Conviction point when violence turns out to be the only thing that resolves a problem after every other approach failed.
Another point comes from persuading a fellow hunter that the Wayward’s plan of destruction is the right one, or from finding information that supports the Wayward’s grand scheme.
Optional rules take a point away when the Wayward fails to hurt a monster, betrays or loses track of the personal crusade, or sees a problem solved by means that run against it.
Only one such gain counts per game session, however many of the triggers occur.

title: Wayward derangements
summary: Personality disorders as the typical Wayward madness.

claims.text: Waywards are bent out of true from the moment of imbuing, so serious mental illness is a constant risk for the creed.
Their usual afflictions are deep personality disorders such as antisocial and borderline personality disorder, rather than small phobias or neuroses.
A Storyteller may give a bonus to a player who works the derangement into the Wayward’s goal for the hunt instead of fighting it.

title: Deviance
summary: The edge path of the Waywards.

claims.text: Deviance is the Wayward edge path, shaped to fit the Wayward outlook and unlike the paths of the other creeds.
Several of its edges look like gifts meant to help other hunters that went wrong, which hints that Waywards were meant for some other purpose.
A hunter of another creed can manifest a Deviance edge, though few even know the Waywards exist.

title: Impart
summary: A Deviance edge that switches on second sight in other hunters.

claims.text: The player rolls Perception + Vision at difficulty 6, and each success turns on the second sight of one other hunter within a number of yards equal to five times the Wayward’s Vision.
Those affected spend no Conviction for the sight but gain none of the usual protection from mind, body and emotion control unless they activate their own second sight.
Impart takes one action, works once per scene and lasts for the rest of the scene even if the recipients move away.

title: Forewarn
summary: A Deviance edge that acts as a danger sense.

claims.text: Forewarn is always active: the Storyteller rolls Wits + Vision at difficulty 7 in secret whenever danger may be close.
Outside combat, each success warns the hunter about one turn before a hazard such as a rotten floor or a hidden trap.
Before an attack, the successes go either to initiative next turn or to a dodge, block or parry roll, as the player chooses.
It says only that something bad is coming, not what, and Conviction cannot be risked on it.

title: Enrage
summary: A Deviance edge that drives other hunters into a killing rage.

claims.text: The player rolls Manipulation + Vision at difficulty 6; each success lets the Wayward push one other hunter within Vision yards into a berserk rage.
Those affected attack the enemy violently, and even gentle hunters may come round surrounded by dead monsters and people alike.
The edge may once have been meant to rally allies like a war leader, but in a broken mind it spreads bloodlust instead.

title: Questioning the dead
summary: A Deviance edge that forces the dead to answer truthfully.

claims.text: The hunter spends a full action locking gazes with a corpse or undead creature, then spends one Conviction and rolls Perception + Vision at difficulty 8; each success allows one question that scene.
It works on corpses and on the walking dead such as vampires, zombies and ghosts, and the answers are heard as whispers in the hunter’s mind.
The dead can only give what they believe to be true, a very old or powerful undead may resist with a Willpower roll at difficulty 6, and a corpse with no eyes or head cannot be asked.

title: Torture and Poison
summary: Two new Skills common among Waywards.

claims.text: Torture and Poison are new Skills that Waywards often have, though other creeds may learn them with Storyteller approval.
Hiding the use of poison on a victim is a resisted roll of Wits + Poison against Intelligence + Medicine, both at difficulty 6.

title: Homemade weapons
summary: Rules for designing and building improvised weapons.

claims.text: Building a scratch-made weapon starts with a design stage that settles what it is made of and how it does damage.
The materials set the most damage dice the weapon can deal, and that cap can never be more than twice the builder’s Crafts rating, or 1 without Crafts.
A construction stage and a chart for melee and ranged designs follow, along with tables for improvised melee, chemical, explosive and incendiary weapons.

title: Signs of the Righteous
summary: Marks that Waywards draw or carve on themselves for strength.

claims.text: At Vision 4 a Wayward begins to sense the meaning of certain symbols, and learns one more for each Vision point above 4.
To use a sign, the Wayward draws the mark on the skin or concentrates on one already worn; it costs three Conviction and lasts a number of days equal to Vision.
The benefit ends early if the mark is smudged, soaked or covered, and only one sign can be active at a time.
Painful ways of marking may cost a level of bashing damage that cannot be soaked, and they usually leave scars.
